      <content name="FullSummary"><p>The urinary system is the body's drainage system for removing wastes and extra water. It includes two kidneys, two ureters, a bladder, and a urethra. Urinary tract infections (UTIs) are the second most common type of infection in the body.</p><p>You may have a UTI if you notice:</p><ul><li>Pain or burning when you urinate</li><li>Fever, tiredness, or shakiness</li><li>An urge to urinate often</li><li>Pressure in your lower belly </li><li>Urine that smells bad or looks cloudy or reddish</li><li>Pain in your back or side below the ribs</li></ul><p>People of any age or sex can get UTIs. But about four times as many women get UTIs as men. You're also at higher risk if you have diabetes, need a tube to drain your bladder, or have a spinal cord injury.</p><p>If you think you have a UTI it is important to see your doctor. Your doctor can tell if you have a UTI with a urine test.  Treatment is with antibiotics. </p><p>NIH: National Institute of Diabetes and Digestive and Kidney Diseases</p></content>
